newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada building permits rise 9.3 pct in April.
newsitem.headline: Canada building permits rise 9.3 pct in April.

text.p: The value of Canadian building permits issued in April rose 9.3 percent to C$2.72 billion, seasonally adjusted, from March, Statistics Canada said on Monday.
April Month pct chg Yr pct change
Economists surveyed by Reuters had forecast on average a month-on-month rise of 3.0 percent after a 5.0 percent fall in March.

Statistics Canada said the value of residential permits fell for the second straight month, but it was more than offset by a surge in non-residential construction intentions, which hit their highest level in almost seven years.
The decrease in residential permits coincided with mortgage rates reaching their highest level in seven months, StatsCan said.
Provincially, British Columbia was the major contributor to the decline in the residential sector in April, falling 13.5 percent, the federal agency said.
As for the non-residential sector, commercial intentions rose by 14.5 percent to C$604 million, while institutional building plans by governments remained unchanged, said StatsCan.
Building permits are an early indicator of future demand for labour and material by construction and contruction-related industries.
According to the Canada Mortgage and Housing Corporation, about 95 percent of the residential building permits issued translate into actual housing starts.
